title: Aos Sí
extract: In Irish and Scottish folklore, the Aos Sí (Irish: aes sídhe) are the supernatural race comparable to the fairies or elves of other traditions. The term is the Irish for 'folk of the sídhe' — the burial mounds or ancient tumuli of Ireland. The word sídhe (singular) is the modern Irish reflex of Old Irish síde, which is in turn the dative singular form of síd, meaning 'a fairy mound or hill'. The word síd derives from proto-Celtic *sīdos, meaning 'abode' or 'seat', which is also the source of the Latin word sēdēs and the Greek word hedos. According to the medieval Irish tradition, the Tuatha Dé Danann were the fifth and last of the mythological races to invade Ireland. After their defeat by the Milesians, the Tuatha Dé Danann withdrew into the sídhe and became the Aos Sí. The Aos Sí can move between their world and the mortal world at will, particularly at Samhain (1 November) and Beltane (1 May).
